records.place: Escherndorf on the Main, in the Maindreieck, Franken

wine.name: Escherndorfer Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from Am Lumpen 1655, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Escherndorf
wine.sites: Am Lumpen 1655, the heart of the Escherndorfer Lump: a slope of about sixty per cent facing south, opening on the valley of the Main like an amphitheatre, on shell limestone, with vines more than thirty five years old.
wine.making: The grapes are selected in the vineyard and pressed very gently. By the house's own sheet the must settles naturally and ferments with its own wild yeasts, no cultured yeast added, and the wine rests on its fine lees until the end of the following July before it is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Lemon peel, kumquat and ripe pear over a peppery, herbal note and a faint bitterness of almond skin, with a salty, stony finish; dry and firm, built on acidity rather than breadth.
wine.ageing: Open and precise on release, it gains honey, nut and dried herbs over five to ten years and keeps longer in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage, named for the year the field name was first recorded.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Dry by the legal measure, as every Grosses Gewächs must be.

records.table: Horst Sauer's Escherndorfer Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG comes from the steep, south facing heart of the Lump, on shell limestone above a bend of the Main. Wild yeasts and long lees give a dry, salty Silvaner of pear and kumquat.
records.story: Escherndorf sits beside a tight loop of the Main, and above the village the Lump climbs in a steep, south facing amphitheatre of shell limestone. Its heart takes its name from a document: by the VDP's account the field name Am Lumpen first appears in a description of goods and statutes in 1655, and the year became part of the name of the Grosse Lage. As the house tells it, the Sauer family had tended vines on the Lump for many generations, but the estate that carries the founder's name is young. In 1971 the founder and his father planted the Hütte parcel on the Lump, the first vineyard the founder set himself, and the estate grew from a small start on the Lump and the neighbouring Fürstenberg. It joined the VDP in 2001. The library knows it as the Franken estate a candidate should name for serious dry Silvaner, and for botrytis wines of rare clarity from the same slope. Another Escherndorf house, Rainer Sauer, bottles a wine from the same site under the same name, so the first name on the label matters. For a sommelier this is the place to learn what shell limestone and a steep southern slope make of Franken's own grape.

traps: Weingut Rainer Sauer is a separate Escherndorf estate that also bottles an Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG; read the first name.
Am Lumpen 1655 is the Grosse Lage at the heart of the Escherndorfer Lump, not a different village or a Grosslage.
The Lump is shell limestone, Muschelkalk, not the red sandstone of the Mainviereck or the gypsum Keuper of the Steigerwald.

cards.back: The year the field name Am Lumpen was first written down, in a description of goods and statutes.

cards.back: Shell limestone, on a steep slope facing south above a bend of the Main.

questions.q: A guest asks how Horst Sauer's Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG is fermented. Which answer is right?
opts: With its own wild yeasts, then long on fine lees
With a cultured yeast in new barriques
On its skins for weeks, like a red wine
With added sugar to leave it sweet
questions.exp: The house's sheet gives natural settling, wild yeasts and fine lees until July; no cultured yeast is added, and a Grosses Gewächs is always dry.

questions.q: In which year did Weingut Horst Sauer join the VDP?
questions.exp: The VDP gives membership from 2001; 1971 is the year the Hütte parcel was planted and 1655 the year the field name was written down.

Boutinot: Horst Sauer Escherndorf am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG

report: The label form is Escherndorf am Lumpen 1655 on the house's shop, Falstaff and the importer; the plan's Escherndorfer form is kept in the name as the lint asks, and the library's Escherndorfer Lump Silvaner GG is the older, wider name.

1655 as the first record of the field name rests on the VDP's site page and the house; the VDP calls the document a description of goods and statutes, a trade account calls it a wine tax record, so the record follows the VDP.
The founder and his daughter are living and are not named; the father who planted the Hütte with him in 1971 is not named either, his dates unknown.
Founded is empty: the house says it was founded by the founder on a small holding but gives no year, and 1971 is the planting of a parcel.

Left out for want of a source: the year of the first bottling under the house's own name, the vessel (steel or cask) for the GG, and any claim that the house was first to make dry Lump Silvaner of this rank.
The serving and ageing lines follow the Codex's service reference and the trade's general reading; no vintage figure is used.

wine.name: Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Stein-Berg, a VDP.Grosse Lage within the Würzburger Stein
wine.sites: The Stein-Berg, a curved VDP Grosse Lage of the Würzburger Stein above the city, facing south to south east at 210 to 285 metres, mostly terraced and steep, on weathered shell limestone with clay loam that throws light back onto the vines.
wine.making: By the foundation's own account its leading wines mature in large wooden casks in the cellar beneath the hospital, some of them coopered from oak of the foundation's own forests and fitted with cooling plates to steady the fermentation; the Grosses Gewächs is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Yellow pear, forest honey and dried fig over smoke and crushed stone, with the grip of shell limestone; dry, full and tactile, with a long, savoury finish.
wine.ageing: Firm when young, it opens after three or four years and gains honey and smoke over a decade and more in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour or let it open in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The city and the Grosse Lage within the Stein, the name the GG carries by the 2020 vintage.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
The wine estate of the charitable foundation of 1576, which pays for its hospital and care homes.

records.table: The Juliusspital is the Würzburg charity founded in 1576 whose vineyards were given to pay for its hospital, and its Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG comes from shell limestone terraces above the city. Matured in large casks, it is dry and full, with pear, honey and smoke.
records.story: On 12 March 1576 Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn (1545 to 1617), Prince Bishop of Würzburg from 1573, laid the foundation stone of a great hospital with an almshouse and an orphanage, and in 1579 he endowed it. He gave it farms, forests and vineyards so that it could pay its own way, and that design has held: by the foundation's own account the proceeds of its agriculture, its forests and its wine estate finance its hospital and its care for the old and the sick. A stone charter carved in 1576 shows the gifts, and Wines of Germany notes a Bocksbeutel among them. The cellar under the hospital dates from the foundation, as the house tells it, and holds some two hundred and twenty large wooden casks for the wines of its leading sites. The chief of those is the Würzburger Stein, the shell limestone hill above the city whose wine was long called Steinwein, its greater part shared among the Juliusspital, the Bürgerspital and the Staatlicher Hofkeller. Silvaner is the house's main grape, and its Grosses Gewächs from the Stein, labelled Stein-Berg by the 2020 vintage, is its reading of the city's own hill. For a sommelier it is Würzburg Silvaner as a charity has made it for four and a half centuries.

others.name: Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg Silvaner GG
others.note: A Silvaner Grosses Gewächs from Iphofen in the Steigerwald, the site named for the founder.

others.name: Würzburg Stein Silvaner Erste Lage
others.note: The dry Silvaner from the wider Stein, ranked a step below the Grosses Gewächs.

others.name: Würzburg Stein-Berg Riesling GG
others.note: Riesling from the same Grosse Lage, beside the Silvaner.

traps: The Juliusspital was founded by a Prince Bishop in 1576; the Bürgerspital by a patrician couple in 1316. Do not swap the dates.
From about the 2020 vintage the Stein GG reads Würzburg Stein-Berg; it is the same hill, not a new village or a different estate.
The Julius-Echter-Berg is at Iphofen, on gypsum Keuper in the Steigerwald, not in Würzburg.

cards.front: Who founded the Juliusspital in Würzburg, and in what year?
cards.back: Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn, Prince Bishop of Würzburg, in 1576.

cards.front: Juliusspital's Silvaner GG: on what soil does its Würzburg site grow?
cards.back: Weathered shell limestone with clay loam, on the terraced Stein above the city.

questions.q: A guest sees Würzburg Stein-Berg on a recent bottle of Juliusspital's Silvaner GG. What does Stein-Berg name?
opts: A Grosse Lage within the Würzburger Stein
A village east of Würzburg
A sweet Prädikat level
The foundation's second label
questions.exp: The VDP lists the Stein-Berg as a Grosse Lage of the Stein above Würzburg; it is a vineyard, not a village or a sweetness level.

questions.q: Why did Julius Echter give the Juliusspital vineyards, farms and forests?
opts: So that it could pay for its hospital
To supply wine to the Bishop's court
To settle a debt to the city
To train monks in winegrowing
questions.exp: The endowment was meant to keep the hospital, almshouse and orphanage, and the estate's proceeds finance the foundation's care; it was not a court supply.

sources.title: Deutsche Biographie: Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn
Falstaff: Juliusspital Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG

report: The plan names the wine Würzburger Stein Silvaner GG; Falstaff and wein.plus print Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG from about the 2020 or 2021 vintage, and the VDP lists the Stein-Berg as the Grosse Lage. The name keeps the plan's words; the label term and a trap explain the newer form. No source said when or why the name changed.

The Stein rather than the Julius-Echter-Berg as the lead Silvaner is the plan's choice; the house makes GGs from both and no source ranks one over the other, so a swap to the Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg could be argued and is not proposed.
Julius Echter's dates are the Deutsche Biographie's, 18 March 1545 to 9 September 1617; the foundation stone of 12 March 1576 and the endowment of 1579 are the foundation's own history.
The cellar dating from 1576 and the 220 casks are the house's own account, with the importer for the cellar; a cask coopered from the foundation's own oak is the house's news page.

Left out for want of a source: hand picking, the fermenting yeast, the length of the cask ageing for the GG, the region record's claim of Lump holdings, and any size of the estate (volatile in any case).

wine.name: Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Stein-Harfe, a VDP.Grosse Lage in sole ownership
wine.sites: The Stein-Harfe, in the heart of the Würzburger Stein and held by the Bürgerspital alone: a steep slope of weathered shell limestone, named for the harp its diagonal path and rows draw when seen from the city.
wine.making: By the house's own sheets the grapes stay long on their skins before pressing, the must ferments with its own yeasts in Stück, the large traditional oak casks of German cellars, and the wine then rests on its fine lees in wood before it is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Quince, yellow apple and dried herbs over wet stone and a smoky, salty note; dense and concentrated for Silvaner, dry, with a fine bitter edge and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Closed for its first years, it opens after four or five and keeps well over a decade, gaining honey, smoke and herbs.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour, or pour it slowly; a white wine glass.

label.means: The city and the Grosse Lage in the Stein that the Bürgerspital owns alone.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Dry by the legal measure, as every Grosses Gewächs must be.

records.table: The Bürgerspital is Würzburg's older charity, founded in 1316, and its Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG comes from a corner of the Stein no other house owns. Fermented with its own yeasts in large casks, it is dense, smoky and salty.
records.story: In 1316 a wealthy Würzburg patrician and his wife gave their property to the city to house the sick and the needy, and the Bürgerspital zum Heiligen Geist grew from that gift, enlarged by later endowments of the city's citizens; its wine estate helps to pay for its care. Its treasure was its share of the Würzburger Stein. By the account of Wines of Germany, Silvaner was first planted in the Stein in 1665, by a Cistercian abbot. In 1726 the city council moved against the adulteration of wine: the Bürgerspital's Steinwein of the 1718 vintage was filled in its cellars into Bocksbeutel flasks of about a litre and sealed with the city's seal, and the squat flask became Franken's emblem. The house dates the name of its own corner of the hill to the seventeenth century, when it was written Harpfe, a harp, for the shape its path and rows make seen from the city. The Stein-Harfe is a VDP Grosse Lage held by the Bürgerspital alone, so its dry Silvaner is the one wine of the Stein that only one house can make. For a sommelier it teaches the Stein and the Bocksbeutel in one bottle.

others.name: Würzburger Stein Silvaner 1G Erste Lage
others.note: The dry Silvaner from the house's wider holding in the Stein, ranked a step below the Grosses Gewächs.

traps: The Bürgerspital, founded in 1316 by citizens, is older than the Juliusspital, founded by a Prince Bishop in 1576.
The Würzburger Stein is shared by several houses; the Stein-Harfe within it is the Bürgerspital's alone.
The Bocksbeutel decree of 1726 sealed Steinwein of the 1718 vintage; the flask is the region's, not one house's bottle.

cards.front: Bürgerspital's Stein-Harfe: what gave the vineyard its name?
cards.back: Its diagonal path and rows look like a harp seen from Würzburg; it was written Harpfe in the seventeenth century.

cards.front: In 1726 Würzburg's council ordered Steinwein sealed in which flask, and in whose cellars?
cards.back: The Bocksbeutel, in the cellars of the Bürgerspital, from the 1718 vintage.

questions.q: A guest asks why the Bürgerspital's Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG names a site no other house prints. Why?
opts: The Bürgerspital owns the Stein-Harfe alone
The name is a cooperative's
The site lies outside the Stein
It is a brand for wine bought in
questions.exp: The VDP and the house list the Stein-Harfe as a Grosse Lage in the Bürgerspital's sole ownership, in the heart of the Stein; it is a vineyard, not a brand.

questions.q: In which year was the Bürgerspital zum Heiligen Geist founded in Würzburg?
questions.exp: A patrician couple endowed it in 1316; 1576 is the Juliusspital's founding, 1665 Silvaner's first planting in the Stein and 1726 the Bocksbeutel decree.

Bürgerspital Weingut: Würzburger Stein-Harfe, VDP.Grosse Lage
Bürgerspital Weingut: Würzburger Stein-Harfe Silvaner GG trocken

report: The founders are described, not named: Wikipedia and Wines of Germany name Johannes von Steren and his wife Mergardis, but Steren's dates (about 1270 to 1329) are in one source only.

The 1726 decree and the 1718 vintage rest on Wines of Germany and the house's own account through Tageskarte; Wines of Germany says one litre, Tageskarte one Mass of about 1.22 litres, so the record says about a litre.
Silvaner in the Stein in 1665 by a Cistercian abbot is Wines of Germany with the house's Stein page; the abbot's name is left out for want of his dates.
Left out: Wines of Germany's note that the cellar holds a Steinwein of 1540, since the famous 1540 Steinwein is elsewhere tied to the royal cellar and the claim needs a second source.
The plan's sweet Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese is not in others: no source read confirmed a sweet Stein-Harfe Riesling under that name.
The Stück is not given a size: no source read stated the capacity of the house's casks.

records.place: Bürgstadt on the Main, in the Mainviereck, Franken

wine.name: Bürgstadter Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Hundsrück, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Bürgstadt
wine.grapes: Spätburgunder, the German name for Pinot Noir, alone.
wine.sites: The Hundsrück at Bürgstadt: a steep slope facing south at 170 to 230 metres, on weathered red to orange Buntsandstein, red sandstone that is iron rich, stony and free draining.
wine.making: Fermented on its skins in open wooden vats, with a share of whole bunches that varies with the vintage, then basket pressed. It matures for between twelve and twenty months, by the house's pages, in Burgundian barrels of 228 litres, rests long on its lees, clears in the barrel and is bottled unfiltered.
wine.glass: Red cherry, redcurrant and wild strawberry over cloves, forest floor and a smoky, stony edge; firm, fine tannin, bright acidity and a long, spiced finish.
wine.ageing: Tight for its first five years, it opens slowly and keeps well beyond a decade in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 15 to 16 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Burgundy glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage, a name restored to its own site in 2010.
Pinot Noir, under its German name.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Rudolf Fürst's Bürgstadter Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG is Pinot Noir from a steep slope of red sandstone on the Main in the west of Franken. Fermented in open vats and aged in Burgundian barrels, it is firm and spiced, so decant it.
records.story: The Fürst family has been recorded as winegrowers in Bürgstadt, on the Main in the west of Franken, since 1638, by its own history. The Hundsrück above the village is older on paper: the VDP records that it was assessed for tax in 1564. The wine law of 1971 folded it into the larger Centgrafenberg, and the name left the labels for nearly four decades. In 1979 the family built a new estate house among the vines of the Centgrafenberg, and in the years that followed it became one of the German pioneers of red wine raised in small Burgundian barrels. Its plots on the iron rich red sandstone of the hill gave Spätburgunder that made the Mainviereck known as red wine country, far from the Ahr and Baden. Since 2010 the VDP has listed the Hundsrück again as a site of its own, and the house calls it its flagship site, the one that gives its most powerful and spicy Spätburgunder each year. By 2016, as a trade profile on the house's site tells it, the family was using more whole bunches. For a sommelier the wine is the answer to a question the exam asks: where else in Germany Pinot Noir grows on red sandstone.

others.name: Bürgstadter Centgrafenberg Spätburgunder GG
others.note: The Grosses Gewächs from the larger hill around the estate house, also red sandstone.

others.name: Klingenberger Schlossberg Spätburgunder GG
others.note: From the steep terraces of Klingenberg down the Main.

others.name: Bürgstadter Centgrafenberg Frühburgunder
others.note: From the early ripening mutation of Pinot Noir, a speciality of the house.

traps: The Hundsrück at Bürgstadt is a vineyard in Franken, not the Hunsrück hills between the Mosel and the Nahe.
Bürgstadt lies in the Mainviereck on red sandstone, not on the shell limestone of Würzburg.
Spätburgunder is Pinot Noir; Frühburgunder is its early ripening mutation, a different wine of the same house.

cards.front: Rudolf Fürst's Hundsrück: on what rock does the vineyard grow?
cards.back: Weathered red to orange Buntsandstein, iron rich red sandstone, on a steep slope facing south.

cards.front: When did the Hundsrück lose its own name, and when did the VDP restore it?
cards.back: It was folded into the Centgrafenberg by the wine law of 1971 and listed again as its own site from 2010.

questions.q: A guest asks how Fürst's Hundsrück Spätburgunder GG is raised. Which description fits the house's pages?
opts: Open wooden vats, then Burgundian barrels
Stainless steel, then bottled young
Carbonic maceration in sealed tanks
Concrete eggs, then large old casks only
questions.exp: The house ferments its reds on the skins in open wooden vats and ages them twelve to twenty months in 228 litre Burgundian barrels; steel and early bottling are wrong.

questions.q: Since when has the Fürst family been recorded as winegrowers in Bürgstadt, by its own history?
questions.exp: The family dates its winegrowing in Bürgstadt to 1638; 1564 is the Hundsrück's tax record, 1971 the law that merged it and 1979 the new estate house.

sources.title: Wines of Germany: Weingut Rudolf Fürst, Bürgstadt am Main

report: The Hundsrück as the house's flagship rests on the house's own pages and two trade accounts; the plan's pick stands.
Founded is empty: the family's record from 1638 is a first record, and 1979 is the building of the estate house, not a founding.
The family members who run the estate are living and are not named; Rudolf Fürst, whose name the house carries, is not given dates, since none were found.
Barrel time is twelve to twenty months on the house's German cellar page and thirteen to eighteen on its English page, so the record says between twelve and twenty, hedged as the house's pages.
Sources disagree on whether the Hundsrück lies within the Centgrafenberg or beside it; the record follows the VDP: merged in 1971, its own site again from 2010.
Left out for want of a second source: the first vintage bottled under the Hundsrück name, any share of new oak, the share of whole bunches for this wine, and the Klingenberger Schlossberg's soil.

records.place: Castell, on the western edge of the Steigerwald, Franken

wine.name: Casteller Schlossberg Silvaner GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Schlossberg, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Castell in sole ownership
wine.sites: The Schlossberg below the castle at Castell, on the western edge of the Steigerwald: Keuper clay with gypsum, alabaster and shale, held by the estate alone and planted to Silvaner.
wine.making: By the house's own sheets the grapes are given a short contact on their skins before pressing, the must ferments spontaneously with its own yeasts, and the wine matures in casks of Casteller wood, oak from the estate's own forests, before it is bottled dry.
wine.glass: Green pear, hay and white pepper over chalk dust and a salty note; dry, robust and spiced, with texture from the cask and a long, firm finish.
wine.ageing: Firm in youth, it opens after three to five years; the house gives it a span of ten to thirty years.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour or let it open in the glass; a white wine glass.

label.means: The village and the Grosse Lage below the castle, owned by the estate alone.
GG: a dry wine of the VDP from a vineyard it ranks Grosse Lage.
Franken's grape, called Österreicher at Castell when it was first planted there.

records.table: The Castell estate in the Steigerwald dates its first Silvaner to the foot of its own Schlossberg in 1659, and its Casteller Schlossberg Silvaner GG grows on that slope, on gypsum Keuper. Wild fermented in casks of its own oak, it is robust, peppery and salty.
records.story: The family of Castell traces its line to an ancestor recorded in 1057, and its village lies on the western edge of the Steigerwald, where the vines grow on gypsum Keuper. The house dates its own winegrowing to 1224, when the counts deeded property to the monastery of Ebrach, and the VDP tells of a division of the counts' lands about 1266 that first named Castell's chief vineyards, the Schlossberg below the castle among them. Then came the entry the house keeps as its charter. On 6 April 1659, by the account of the house and of Wines of Germany, twenty five Austrian cuttings were set at the foot of the Schlossberg: Silvaner, long called Österreicher. A purchase record in the princely archive holds the entry, and by its own account the house is the home of German Silvaner, its first recorded planting. The Schlossberg is held by the estate alone and ranked a VDP Grosse Lage, planted to Silvaner. Its Grosses Gewächs carries the whole story in one bottle: the grape, the slope where the house says it was first set in Germany, and the family that set it. For a sommelier it is the wine to pour when a guest asks where Silvaner's German life began.

others.name: Casteller Hohnart Silvaner Erste Lage
others.note: A dry Silvaner from a second Castell site, wild fermented and aged a year on its lees in Castell oak.

others.name: Casteller Kugelspiel Silvaner
others.note: A Castell Silvaner partly raised in wooden casks, partly in steel.

traps: The Fürstlich Castell'sches Domänenamt of the Steigerwald has nothing to do with Rudolf Fürst of Bürgstadt; Fürstlich means princely.
Castell grows on gypsum Keuper in the Steigerwald, not on the shell limestone of Würzburg and Escherndorf.
Castell dates German Silvaner to 1659; the Würzburger Stein's first Silvaner is dated 1665. Keep the two apart.

cards.front: Castell's Schlossberg Silvaner GG: what was planted at the foot of the Schlossberg on 6 April 1659?
cards.back: Twenty five Austrian cuttings, Silvaner, which the house holds to be the grape's first recorded planting in Germany.

cards.front: On what soil does the Casteller Schlossberg grow?
cards.back: Keuper clay with gypsum, alabaster and shale, on the western edge of the Steigerwald.

questions.q: A guest asks what the casks for the Casteller Schlossberg Silvaner GG are made from. What does the house say?
opts: Oak from the estate's own forests
Acacia from the Danube
Chestnut from the Ardennes
Concrete lined with glass
questions.exp: The house matures the GG in casks of Casteller wood, oak from its own forests; acacia and chestnut are other cask woods, not Castell's.

questions.q: By the house's account, in which year was the first Silvaner planted at Castell?
questions.exp: The cuttings were set on 6 April 1659; 1224 is the house's first record of winegrowing, 1266 the division naming its sites and 1665 the Stein's first Silvaner.

sources.title: Castell: Schlossberg Silvaner GG, VDP.Grosse Lage

report: The planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's claim, borne out by Wines of Germany and the importer; both describe twenty five Austrian cuttings at the foot of the Schlossberg, recorded in the princely archive. Told hedged as the house's account.

The official who recorded the 1659 planting and the count of the day are not named: a Franconian source names Johann Georg Körner, another names a Count Wolfgang Georg, and no dates were found for either.
Winegrowing from 1224 is the house's own date, with Wikipedia's deed to Ebrach; another house page says 1266, the VDP's division of the counts' lands. Both are told as what each source says.
Founded is empty: neither 1057 (an ancestor's first record), 1224 nor 1266 is a founding of the estate.
The house now styles itself Castell or Fürst Castell on its pages; the plan's name is kept.
Left out for want of a source: the date the counts became princes, hand picking, and the length of cask ageing for the GG; the princely family is told with no living name.
